newsitem.title: USA: Detroit Edison Nov power sales up 2.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Detroit Edison Nov power sales up 2.5 pct.

text.p: Detroit Edison, citing cold weather and a growing customer base, said Wednesday its November electricity sales rose 2.5 percent over the same month a year ago.
Sales to customers in southeastern Michigan totaled 3.71 billion kilowatthours (kWh) last month, compared with 3.62 billion kWh in November 1995, the company said in a statement.
Sales to residential customers rose 9.0 percent in November to 1.03 billion, due in part to 23,000 more residential customers than they had a year ago.
Commercial sales rose 5.4 percent to 1.45 billion kWh, while industrial sales fell 5.3 percent to 1.11 billion kWh.
Year-to-date, the company's sales in southeastern Michigan through end-November rose 0.9 percent compared with the first 11 months of 1995.
Total sales for the month, including sales to other utilities, rose 1.3 percent.
Year-to-date, Detroit Edison's total electricity sales slipped 1.0 percent compared with the same 1995 period.
Detroit Edison, a subsidiary of DTE Energy Co, serves more than two million customers in souteast Michigan.
